questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the PSLV-C62 mission of 12 January 2026:
1. The anomaly occurred in the solid third stage.
2. The second stage of the PSLV uses a solid rocket motor.
3. It was the second PSLV failure in a row, after PSLV-C61 in May 2025, which also had a third-stage anomaly.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: PSLV-C62, the 64th PSLV flight, lost stability near third-stage burnout and could not reach orbit, so EOS-N1 (Anvesha) and 15 co-passenger satellites were lost. The PSLV's second stage is a liquid stage using the Vikas engine, so statement 2 is wrong. PSLV-C61 (EOS-09) had also failed on a third-stage (PS3) anomaly.
questions.s: India TV News, 12 Jan 2026; Vision IAS

questions.q: ISRO Chairman V. Narayanan said on 30 January 2026 that the Gaganyaan crewed flight is planned for 2027. How many uncrewed missions are to precede the crewed flight?
questions.e: The Gaganyaan programme plans three uncrewed missions before the crewed flight, with astronauts known as Gaganyatri.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's first private Earth Observation constellation:
1. It will consist of 12 satellites covering optical, multispectral, SAR and hyperspectral imaging.
2. The investment is Rs 1,200 crore over five years.
3. IN-SPACe is the commercial arm of ISRO.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A Pixxel-led consortium (with Piersight Space, Satsure Analytics India and Dhruva Space) signed the agreement with IN-SPACe under a public-private partnership. IN-SPACe is the nodal agency that authorises, regulates and promotes private space activity; NSIL is ISRO's commercial arm.

questions.q:
DRDO's Defence Research and Development Laboratory (DRDL) ground-tested a full-scale, actively cooled scramjet combustor for more than 12 minutes in January 2026. Consider the following statements about scramjet engines:
1. They operate efficiently at hypersonic speeds above Mach 5 and allow supersonic combustion.
2. They have no rotating compressor.
3. They can produce thrust at zero air speed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A scramjet compresses air using the vehicle's forward motion and has no rotating compressor or turbine, but it cannot produce thrust at zero air speed, so it needs a rocket or turbojet booster to reach operating speed. The test supports the Hypersonic Cruise Missile programme.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about reusable rocket technology:
1. Reusable rockets aim to recover the first stage, which holds the most expensive engines, avionics and tanks.
2. More than 90 per cent of a rocket's liftoff mass is payload.
3. ISRO is pursuing a winged Reusable Launch Vehicle (RLV) and stage-recovery systems.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: More than 90 per cent of liftoff mass is propellant and tanks, with payload under 4 per cent, which is why launches are costly. Falcon 9's first stage lands using engine re-ignition (retro-propulsion). India's two routes are a winged shuttle-like RLV landing on a runway and stage recovery using drag and retro-propulsion.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements on ISRO's next-generation launch vehicle and the space sector:
1. The Next-Generation Launch Vehicle is presented as a partially reusable vehicle able to carry up to 30 tonnes to low Earth orbit.
2. IN-SPACe launched a technology adoption fund to help firms bridge prototypes and scalable products.
3. India has a comprehensive national space law.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Commentary noted that India lacks a comprehensive space law, leaving ISRO to act as fallback regulator, and called for statutory authority for ISRO, IN-SPACe and NSIL. The NGLV is a high-capacity, partially reusable design, and IN-SPACe's fund targets import reduction.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about asteroid 2025 MN45:
1. It was discovered in the first images of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory in Chile.
2. It rotates once every 1.88 hours.
3. It lies in the main belt between Mars and Jupiter.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The asteroid, about 710 m across, rotates once every 1.88 minutes, making it the fastest-spinning asteroid found with a diameter over 500 m. The Rubin Observatory's 8.4 m Simonyi Survey Telescope has the world's largest digital camera (3,200 megapixels).

questions.q: Astronomers at ARIES used the Devasthal Fast Optical Telescope and NASA's TESS to study a low-mass W Ursae Majoris star in January 2026. Such a star is
o: a pair of neutron stars orbiting each other every few years
a single pulsating variable star with a period of several weeks
an eclipsing contact binary whose two stars share an outer atmosphere, with an orbital period of about 0.25 to 1 day
a black hole feeding on a distant companion
questions.e: W UMa stars are tight contact binaries with orbital periods of about 0.25 to 1 day. The study found strong magnetic activity and star spots. ARIES (Aryabhatta Research Institute of Observational Sciences) is under the Department of Science and Technology.

questions.q: According to the standard composition of the universe, cited in the context of a dark matter map made with the James Webb Space Telescope, which one of the following is correct?
o: Normal matter 5 per cent, dark matter 27 per cent, dark energy 68 per cent
Normal matter 27 per cent, dark matter 5 per cent, dark energy 68 per cent
Normal matter 5 per cent, dark matter 68 per cent, dark energy 27 per cent
Normal matter 68 per cent, dark matter 27 per cent, dark energy 5 per cent
questions.e: Dark matter, inferred from its gravitational effects, does not emit, absorb or reflect light. It makes up about 27 per cent of the universe, dark energy about 68 per cent and visible matter only 5 per cent.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Mpemba effect simulation of January 2026:
1. It was done by the Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research, an autonomous body under the Department of Atomic Energy.
2. The Mpemba effect is the paradox that hot water can sometimes freeze faster than cold water.
3. It is named after Tanzanian student Erasto Mpemba, who drew attention to it in 1969.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: JNCASR is an autonomous institute under the Department of Science and Technology, not the Department of Atomic Energy. The simulation, called the first to reproduce the Mpemba effect, suggests water passes through short-lived intermediate molecular states. Aristotle had described the effect in Meteorologica.

questions.q:
A study reported in January 2026 found that the oceans absorbed a record amount of extra heat in 2025. Consider the following statements:
1. The additional heat absorbed was about 23 zettajoules, the highest since records began in the 1960s.
2. Oceans absorb nearly 90 per cent of the excess heat trapped by greenhouse gases.
3. Warmer surface waters increase mixing between ocean layers and raise oxygen supply to the deep sea.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Oceans took up about 23 ZJ of extra heat in 2025 and hold about 90 per cent of the excess heat from greenhouse gases. Warming strengthens stratification, which reduces mixing, lowers oxygen supply to deeper water and cuts nutrient transport, so statement 3 is wrong. Marine heat waves, coral bleaching and stronger cyclones follow.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the blood-red auroral display captured at Hanle in January 2026:
1. It was recorded by the all-sky camera at the Indian Astronomical Observatory.
2. The Hanle Dark Sky Reserve lies at about 4,500 m in the Changthang region of Ladakh.
3. The Reserve is managed by ISRO.
4. It is India's first Dark Sky Reserve, notified in December 2022.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Reserve is managed by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics under the Department of Science and Technology, not ISRO. The other three statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the BSL-4 laboratory whose foundation stone was laid in Gandhinagar in January 2026:
1. It is India's first State-funded BSL-4 laboratory, run by the Gujarat Biotechnology Research Centre.
2. It will be India's first civilian BSL-4 laboratory.
3. Pathogens to be studied include Ebola, Nipah, Marburg, CCHF and Kyasanur Forest Disease.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The National Institute of Virology, Pune already has a civilian BSL-4 lab, so the Gandhinagar facility will be the second civilian one; DRDO operates a defence BSL-4 lab at Gwalior. Union Home Minister Amit Shah laid the foundation stone.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Zycubo (copper histidinate), approved by the US FDA in January 2026:
1. It is the first treatment for Menkes disease in paediatric patients.
2. Menkes disease is caused by a mutation in the ATP7A gene on the X chromosome and impairs copper transport.
3. It mostly affects female infants.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Menkes disease is X-linked recessive, so it mostly affects male infants; males have one X chromosome and no second copy to compensate.

questions.q: Dr Satendra Mangrauthia received a Vigyan Yuva award in 2026 for his work on Kamala. Kamala is
o: a transgenic Bt cotton hybrid with insect resistance
India's first genome-edited rice variety, developed by ICAR
a biofortified wheat rich in zinc and iron
a genetically modified mustard hybrid cleared for commercial sowing
questions.e: Kamala (DRR Dhan 100) is the first genome-edited rice released in India, developed by ICAR. Genome editing alters the plant's own genes, and the SDN-1 route used here introduces no foreign DNA, unlike transgenic crops such as Bt cotton.

questions.q:
Nipah virus infection was confirmed in West Bengal in January 2026. Which of the following statements are correct?
1. The National Institute of Virology, Pune confirmed it in two nurses at a private hospital in Barasat, North 24 Parganas.
2. All 196 traced contacts tested negative.
3. A licensed vaccine against Nipah is available.
4. Fruit bats are the natural reservoir.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
questions.e: There is no licensed vaccine or specific treatment for Nipah. The WHO rated the risk moderate in West Bengal and low nationally. Nipah is a zoonotic virus, first identified in the 1999 Malaysia-Singapore outbreak, with an incubation of 4 to 14 days.
questions.s: UN India (WHO update); Vision IAS, Jan 2026

questions.q: Biomaterials are classed as drop-in, drop-out and novel. Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
questions.e: Drop-in biomaterials are chemically identical to petroleum-based materials and fit existing manufacturing, as bio-PET does. Drop-out biomaterials are chemically different and need new processing or end-of-life systems, as with polylactic acid (PLA). Novel biomaterials offer new properties, such as self-healing materials.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about marine and space biotechnology in India:
1. Seaweed cultivation is modest, at about 70,000 tonnes annually.
2. India imports agar, carrageenan and alginates.
3. India's Exclusive Economic Zone is about 5 million sq km.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India's EEZ is about 2 million sq km, with a coastline of over 11,000 km. Government initiatives include the Blue Economy agenda, the Deep Ocean Mission and the BioE3 policy, and ISRO runs a microgravity biology programme.

questions.q: Shrutlekh, demonstrated by MeitY in January 2026 under BHASHINI, is
o: a tool for detecting deepfake videos on social media
an AI tool for real-time multilingual speech-to-text translation of speeches
a digital locker for storing educational certificates
a chatbot for farmers on mandi prices
questions.e: BHASHINI operates under the National Language Translation Mission, supports over 22 scheduled languages and includes the Bhashadaan crowdsourcing initiative.

questions.q:
The Department of Telecommunications de-licensed part of the 6 GHz band in January 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. The lower half of the band (5,925-6,425 MHz) was de-licensed for indoor use.
2. It enables Wi-Fi 6E and Wi-Fi 7.
3. Use is permitted on moving vehicles and oil rigs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Use of the de-licensed band is prohibited on moving vehicles and oil rigs.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the draft Battery Pack Aadhaar system:
1. Every EV battery pack and industrial battery above 2 kWh gets a 21-character Battery Pack Aadhaar Number and a QR code.
2. It applies to all batteries irrespective of capacity.
3. Static data is stored on the BPAN and dynamic data such as battery health on a central server.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The requirement covers EV batteries and industrial batteries with capacity above 2 kWh, not all batteries. The aim is end-to-end traceability, enabling second-life use and recycling.

questions.q: Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communication technology, which India announced it will roll out, is a system in which
o: vehicles exchange warnings directly with one another without relying on third-party networks such as cellular networks
vehicles communicate only through mobile towers operated by telecom companies
a central traffic control room routes all vehicle messages
vehicles send data only to fixed roadside cameras
questions.e: V2V works across the front, rear and sides of a vehicle, factors in terrain and curves, and strengthens Advanced Driver Assistance Systems by sharing warnings even when a hazard is not visible. The announcement came from the Union Road Transport and Highways Minister.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Military Quantum Mission Policy Framework released by the Chief of Defence Staff:
1. It is aligned with the National Quantum Mission, which has an outlay of about Rs 6,000 crore for 2023-24 to 2030-31.
2. Its core domains are quantum communication, quantum computing, quantum sensing and metrology, and quantum materials and devices.
3. Quantum Key Distribution secures keys through the mathematical complexity of factoring large numbers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The framework seeks joint Tri-Service quantum capability tied to the National Quantum Mission, across four pillars. QKD relies on quantum principles such as entanglement to make keys theoretically unhackable, unlike classical encryption that rests on mathematical difficulty, so statement 3 is wrong. Quantum navigation using atom interferometry can replace vulnerable satellite-based GPS.

questions.q: ACASA-India, launched in January 2026 as the National Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture (NICRA) completed 15 years, is
o: a satellite constellation for monitoring crop residue burning
an app giving farmers real-time mandi prices
a digital Atlas of Climate Adaptation in Indian Agriculture built by the ICAR-led agricultural research system with BISA-CIMMYT
a national registry for agricultural carbon credits
questions.e: ACASA-India is a data-driven platform for location-specific climate adaptation planning in farming, helping agencies judge future investment needs. NICRA was launched by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research in 2011 to build climate resilience and demonstrate resilient technologies on farmers' fields.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) Centres:
1. The World Economic Forum announced five new 4IR Centres, one of them in Andhra Pradesh.
2. It will be the third such centre in India after Mumbai and Telangana.
3. The term Fourth Industrial Revolution was coined by Satya Nadella in 2016.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The term was coined by Klaus Schwab, founder of the World Economic Forum, in 2016. 4IR describes the convergence of digital, physical and biological technologies such as AI, robotics, IoT and quantum computing.
